title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government responded to the 2020 Committee report on AI and Public Standards by acknowledging the importance of responsible AI deployment and outlining steps to enhance oversight, transparency, and accountability. It plans to develop new guidelines, strengthen regulatory frameworks, and collaborate with stakeholders to promote ethical AI practices across public services.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The EU Regulation 2024/1689 sets out uniform rules for the use of artificial intelligence across the bloc, aiming to improve safety, transparency, and accountability. It also amends several existing regulations and directives, updating legal frameworks to better align with AI‑related risks and opportunities.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to protect the integrity and fairness of assessments. The guidance, released after a request from senior education, science, innovation and trade officials, sets out rules and best practices for educators and exam bodies when incorporating AI.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted works, evaluating the legal and ethical implications of their use. It offers guidance on responsible practices to protect both creators’ rights and the development of AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released its response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, acknowledging the urgent need for action on artificial intelligence. The response outlines measures such as increased funding, stronger regulation, and collaborative initiatives to keep the UK a global leader while safeguarding public trust and safety.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and duties of a committee that will review artificial intelligence in relation to public standards, and includes frequently asked questions to clarify the process. It outlines how the committee will assess AI's impact, develop relevant standards, and involve stakeholders to safeguard public interests.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how artificial intelligence should be governed. Their submission offers the CSPL’s perspective on AI regulation and aims to help shape national AI policy.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence influences the rules and approval processes for medical products, ensuring safety, efficacy, and patient protection. It outlines steps for applying the AI White Paper principles to develop and enforce standards that guide the integration of AI technologies in medical devices and treatments.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a plan to use AI to make the defense organization more effective, efficient, trustworthy, and influential. The goal is to become the leading AI‑powered defense force among similarly sized nations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with industry to harness AI for better transport services and efficiency. It also outlines measures to identify, assess and mitigate risks associated with AI use in the sector.
